_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Holding diesel at $4.57/gal — search results this week are genuinely all over the map ($4.58 to $4.80) on conflicting Iran/Strait of Hormuz headlines, some saying the conflict premium is draining out, others saying it just re-escalated. Not putting a new number on your fuel surcharge math until that settles; check your own bill of lading fuel surcharge line before you quote. Underneath the noise, the persistent signal is unchanged: dry van running above contract, flatbed at record highs, Georgia reefer tightening as Florida closes out. That pressure hasn't broken — keep pushing your ask, don't discount into a market that's still tight.

_sourcing.status: Everything carried-forward this cycle, including diesel — demoted from last week's partial-LIVE status because this week's re-verification attempt surfaced three mutually contradictory WebSearch figures instead of a clean corroboration. See refreshBlockers.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: CARRIED-FORWARD, unconfirmed this cycle: still showing $4.57/gal (week ending 2026-07-06, last cycle's partial-live figure). Re-verification was attempted per instructions but WebSearch returned three incompatible readings for the current period instead of agreement: (1) AgriNews + an IndexBox/USDA diesel report, both citing EIA, say national diesel JUMPED 21.8–22c to $4.796 for week ending 2026-07-13 on 'U.S.-Iran conflict re-escalation' / Strait of Hormuz tension resuming ~7/14, with a detailed regional breakdown (CA $6.126, West Coast $5.55, Central Atlantic $5.204, Lower Atlantic $4.748) that reads like a real EIA table; (2) a FleetOwner headline independently repeats that same $4.796/Iran-escalation story, but a DIFFERENT FleetOwner headline in the same search batch reads 'EIA diesel prices drop 9 cents' and another reads 'diesel and gas prices drop for 6th straight week' — same outlet, contradictory headlines; (3) a Freightos 'Hormuz closure' update tells the OPPOSITE causal story — blockade lifted mid-June, conflict premium draining out, diesel on an 8th straight weekly decline to $4.668/gal — while its own headline ('Hormuz closure pushing fuel costs BACK UP') contradicts its own summarized body text; (4) an AJOT/DAT fuel-surcharge item says diesel 'fell 9 cents to $4.58' for the week of 7/12–18, but the identical phrasing and cents-figure also showed up attached to the 7/5–11 week in the same search batch — a strong sign that snippet is a stale/recycled template, not a real distinct weekly reading. Net: a 3-way contradiction (up to $4.80 / down to $4.58 / down to $4.67) with dueling escalation-vs-de-escalation narratives, and no way to check eia.gov directly (still 403 both attempts today). Nothing was promoted. Treat $4.57 as stale, not confirmed current — real risk it has moved either direction; needs a primary-source check next cycle.

_sourcing.blurb: rewritten this cycle to be honest that diesel could NOT be re-confirmed (contradictory WebSearch signals, see dieselPerGal note above) rather than imply a fresh live number; rate-stance coaching carried forward, still backed only by the unverified but persistent trade-press directional signal.
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: Same caveat as the last two cycles, still unresolved: trade press keeps saying dry van spot is above contract for the first time since Feb 2022, flatbed is at a record high, and Southeast reefer is tight (Florida closing, Georgia opening higher). Directionally consistent with the 'up' trend, but every attempt to pin an exact current number has produced internally contradictory WebSearch snippets (see modality note). Do not put into numeric fields until a primary source (dat.com/trendlines or eia.gov) is actually reachable.

refreshBlockers: Re-tested egress first, as instructed: WebFetch to eia.gov (both /petroleum/gasdiesel/ and /dnav/pet/pet_pri_gnd_dcus_nus_w.htm) returned HTTP 403 again today — block is still active, unchanged from the 07-07 and 07-14 attempts (agent proxy status: enabled:true, no relay failures logged, so this is a destination-side 403, not a proxy outage). WebSearch works and returned plenty of results, but this cycle's results were LESS usable than last cycle's: diesel had clean 2-source numeric agreement on 07-14 and got promoted to partial-live; this cycle produced a 3-way contradiction ($4.796 up vs. $4.58 down vs. $4.668 down) with conflicting Iran/Strait-of-Hormuz narratives (one saying the conflict just re-escalated, another saying it eased weeks ago), so diesel was demoted back to carried-forward rather than refreshed. Spot/modality searches were similarly inconsistent (van quoted at both $2.93 and $3.00/mi, reefer at both $3.31 and $3.39/mi for the same week) so those stayed carried-forward as before. Broader web-fetch access (not just search) to a primary source like eia.gov or dat.com/trendlines would resolve this in one fetch instead of guessing between contradictory secondary summaries.
